Rashi on Bava Metzia 72a:10:1.english: He went - the owner of the vineyard.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 72a:10:2.english: He transferred it - As a gift before witnesses.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 72a:10:3.hebrew: לבנו קטן - כדי שלא תהא מכירתו מכירה, שכשיוציא שטר מכירתו, זה יוציא שטר מתנתו. ולא גילה הדבר:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 72a:10:3.english: To his minor son - So that his sale would not be a [valid] sale, for when [the lender] produces his deed of sale, this one [the borrower] will produce his deed of gift. And he did not reveal the matter.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 72a:11:1.hebrew: זוזי - מעות שהוא תובע ממנו, שמוציא עליו שטר, "שמכרת לי כרם שאין שלך, וקבלת מעותיי, וכתבת לי אחריות":
Rashi on Bava Metzia 72a:11:1.english: The dinars - [The] money that he [the buyer] claims from him [the seller], as he produces a deed against him [stating], "You sold me a vineyard that is not yours, and you received my money, and you wrote me a guarantee [of indemnity]."

Rashi on Bava Metzia 72a:11:2.english: [Are they] similar to a loan with a document - For he wrote him a guarantee.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 72a:1:1.hebrew: אית ליה זכיה - דתנן, זכין לקטן בפרק מי שמת (ב"ב דף קנו:):
Rashi on Bava Metzia 72a:1:1.english: He has [the power of] acquisition - For we learned in a Mishnah: One may acquire [property] on behalf of a minor, in the chapter [entitled] Mi Shemet (Bava Batra 156b).

Rashi on Bava Metzia 72a:3:1.hebrew: וזקפן עליו במלוה - לאחר זמן, חישב עמו על הרבית וזוקף הכל ביחד במלוה, וכתב לו שטר עליהם: "כך וכך אני חייב לפלוני":
Rashi on Bava Metzia 72a:3:1.english: And he established them as a loan for him - After some time, [the gentile] calculated the interest with him and establishes all of it together as a loan, and [the borrower] wrote him a promissory note for them: "I owe such-and-such [an amount] to so-and-so."

Rashi on Bava Metzia 72a:3:2.english: And he collects the interest - For from the time of consolidation [into a loan], it is [considered] as collected.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 72a:5:1.hebrew: בין כך ובין כך - אסיפא פליג, וטעמא כדמפרש ואזיל, שלא יאמרו כו':
Rashi on Bava Metzia 72a:5:1.english: Whether [in] this [case] or [in] that [case] - He disagrees with the latter clause [of the baraita], and the reason is as [the Gemara] goes on to explain: "that [people] will not say, etc."

Rashi on Bava Metzia 72a:6:1.english: A [promissory] note in which there is interest - [That is, one] in which it is written: "So-and-so borrowed a maneh from so-and-so at such-and-such interest for such-and-such a time."

Rashi on Bava Metzia 72a:7:1.english: The antedated [notes] - [Dated prior] to the loan.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 72a:7:2.hebrew: פסולין - דבעי למיטרף לקוחות מזמן הכתוב בו, ועדיין לא הלוה, ושטר הלקוחות קודם למלוה, וזה מוציא שטרו והוא קודם, והוא שקר:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 72a:7:2.english: Are not valid - For [the lender] wants to seize [property from] purchasers from the date written in it, when he had not yet lent [the money], and the purchasers' deed precedes the loan, yet this one produces his note and it is earlier, and it is false.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 72a:7:3.hebrew: פסולים - ואינו טורף מן המשועבדין, ואפילו מן המאוחר למלוה:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 72a:7:3.english: [They are] not valid - And [the lender] cannot seize from encumbered [property], even from [property sold] after the loan.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 72a:8:1.hebrew: ר"מ היא - דקניס היתירא אטו איסורא:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 72a:8:1.english: It is Rabbi Meir - For he penalizes that which is permitted on account of that which is prohibited.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 72a:8:2.hebrew: שמא יגבה מן זמן ראשון - דאיכא דלא מסיק אדעתיה לדקדק כל כך בזמן הלואה, לומר למלוה "שטרך מוקדם ומקחי קדם להלואתך":
Rashi on Bava Metzia 72a:8:2.english: Lest he collect from the first date - For there is [one] who does not think to scrutinize the date of the loan so closely, [so as] to say to the lender, "Your document is predated, and my purchase preceded your loan."

Rashi on Bava Metzia 72a:9:2.english: I will hide - I will conceal [it].

Rashi on Bava Metzia 72a:9:3.hebrew: ואמינא לקוחה היא בידי - ואבד שטר המכירה, ואבא מכח חזקה של ג' שנים, דכולי האי לא מצינא למיזדהר בשטרא:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 72a:9:3.english: And I will say: It is purchased in my possession - [and that] the deed of sale was lost, and I will come on the strength of a three-year presumptive ownership, as I cannot guard a deed for that long.

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 72a:11:1.hebrew: אמר אביי לאו היינו דרבי אסי דאמר רבי אסי כו' - תימה: מה ענין דר' אסי לכאן? וי"ל: דהכא לא מיבעיא ליה אי גבי ממשעבדי אי לא, אלא משום דפשיטא ליה דנאמן לומר "פרעתי" משום דלא ניתן ליכתב, ומיבעיא ליה אי לא גבי ממשעבדי כיון דאין השטר מועיל אלא ע"פ הודאתו, או דילמא גבי. ועל זה בא אביי להביא מדרבי אסי: דכי היכי דמודה בשטר מהני הודאתו לגבות ממשעבדי, אע"פ שאם היה אומר "מזויף הוא" היה צריך קיום, ה"נ הכא גבי פרדיסא. ולא שייך כאן לגרוס "אין צריך לקיימו", אלא גרסי': "לאו היינו דרבי אסי, דאמר ר' אסי: מודה בשטר שכתבו, גובה מנכסים משועבדים". ולפי זה, כשמקשה על רבא מההיא ד"לשבח קרקעות", בלא רבא היה יכול להקשות מיד לכ"ע: מ"ש הכא דנאמן לומר "פרעתי", וב"נמצאת שאינו שלו" אינו נאמן כל זמן ששטר מכר בידו? אלא נטר עד לבסוף, ומקשה על רבא מגביית משעבדי השנוי בפירוש בברייתא:
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 72a:11:1.english: Abaye said: Is this not [the same as that of] Rabbi Asi, as Rabbi Asi said, etc. - This is astonishing: what relevance does Rabbi Asi's [statement] have here? And one can answer that here, [the Gemara] is not inquiring whether he can collect from liened property or not [in general]; rather, [it asks this] because it is obvious to it that [the seller] is believed to say "I already paid," since [the deed] was not meant to be written, and [therefore] it is inquiring whether he cannot collect from liened property since the document is effective only on the basis of his admission, or whether he can collect. And regarding this, Abaye comes to bring [a proof] from Rabbi Asi's [statement]: that just as [in the case of] one who admits [that he wrote] a document, his admission is effective to collect from liened property—even though if he had said "It is forged," [the claimant] would have needed verification—so too here regarding the orchard [case]. And it is not appropriate here to read "he does not need to verify it" [in Rabbi Asi's statement]; rather, we read: "Is this not [the same as that of] Rabbi Asi, as Rabbi Asi said: One who admits that he wrote a document, [the creditor] collects from liened property." And according to this, when [the Gemara later] challenges Rava from that [baraita] regarding "improvements to land," even without Rava it could have challenged immediately according to everyone: What is the difference here [in the orchard case], where he is believed to say "I paid," whereas in [the case where a field] "is found not to be his," he is not believed as long as the deed of sale is in [the buyer's] hand? Rather, it waited until the end, and challenges Rava from the collection of liened property, which is explicitly taught in the baraita.

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 72a:6:1.hebrew: שטר שיש בו רבית קונסין אותו ואין גובה לא את הקרן ולא את הרבית - פריב"ם דאין גובה ממשעבדי, אבל מבני חרי גבי ע"פ אותו השטר, דעדים אינם פסולים דאינם עדי חמס, דאין מרויחים כלום בדבר. וקשה, דתניא בתוספתא [פ"ה] דמכלתין: "המוצא שטר שיש בו רבית יקרענו; בא לב"ד יקרעוהו". והשתא אי גבי ביה מבני חרי, אמאי יקרעוהו? ימתינו עד שיגבה בו קודם! וי"ל שאסור להשהותו. מיהו נראה דר"מ קניס לגמרי ולא גבי ביה כלל, כמו שטרי חוב המוקדמים דמוקמינן בסמוך כר"מ; ואף על גב שגם שם פי' בקונטרס דאין פסולין אלא לגבות ממשעבדי, אין נראה, ד"פסולין" משמע דלא גבי ביה כלל. והא דפריך: "נהי דלא גבי מזמן ראשון, ליגבי מזמן שני", הוה מצי למימר נמי: "נהי דלא גבי ממשעבדי, ניגבי מבני חרי", אלא רבותא פריך, דאפי' ממשעבדי ניגבי מזמן שני. ובסמוך דפריך אעובדא דפרדיסא: "אלא הא דאמר רבי יוחנן: גזירה שמא יגבה מזמן ראשון, נימא דלא ניתן ליכתב", ולא משני משום דטעמא דלא ניתן ליכתב לא מהני אלא דלא גבי ממשעבדי — משום דס"ל דודאי מהני לפוסלו לגמרי ולא גבי ביה כלל. והא דלא מיבעיא ליה אלא אי גבי ממשעבדי, אבל מבני חרי פשיטא ליה דגבי אף על גב דלא ניתן להיכתב — התם הוא דפשיטא ליה דגבי, היינו משום שהמוכר היה מודה ללוקח שלא פרע. ועוד נראה דאפי' יש עדים אחרים או שחייב מודה, אפ"ה קניס ר"מ, דהכי משמע דאין גובה קרן דומיא דרבית. ובתוספתא (שם) נמי משמע דאפילו במלוה על פה קניס, דקתני: "המלוה את חבירו ברבית ובא לפני ב"ד, קונסין אותו ואינו גובה לא את הקרן ולא את הרבית, שהיה ר"מ אומר: שטר שיש בו רבית כו'". ובפ' המניח (ב"ק דף ל:) נמי מדמינן לההוא דקנסו גופן משום שבחן דמפסיד גוף הממון, הוא הדין דקניס בגוף המלוה — אע"פ שיש לדחות דהתם עבירה נעשית בגוף הממון יותר מכאן, דכאן עיקר עבירה בשטר, כדאמרינן התם: "משעת כתיבה עבד ליה שומא", ולכך לא קנסו אלא בשטר. ומיהו רבנן נראה דודאי לא קנסו כלל, ומשמע לכאורה דגבי לרבנן בשטר קרן אפילו ממשעבדי, ור"מ נמי לא פליג אלא משום דקניס. ותימה: דאמאי אין העדים פסולים? כיון שעוברים על "לא תשימון" (שמות כב), אע"פ שאין מרויחים יש להם לפסול, מידי דהוה אעבריין אוכל נבילות להכעיס, דקי"ל (סנהדרין דף כז.) כאביי דפסול! והא דלא חשיב להו בפרק זה בורר (סנהדרין דף כד:), ה"נ לא חשיב לוה, אלא הוי בכלל "מלוה הבאה ברבית", כדמפרש התם: "מלוה הבאה ברבית", והוא הדין נמי עדים בכלל. ואין לפרש כגון שאין רבית מפורש בשטר, אלא כתב סתם "פלוני חייב לפלוני מנה" וכללו הקרן עם הרבית והעדים לא ידעו — דא"כ, בסמוך דקאמר ר' יוחנן דמודו רבנן בשטרי חוב המוקדמין גזירה שמא יגבה מזמן ראשון, ה"נ נגזור שמא יגבה רבית בתורת קרן! ואין לומר נמי דכיון שהרבית מפורש בשטר, אין העדים עוברין על "לא תשימון", כיון דיודעין העדים דבית דין לא יגבו על ידם רבית ולכך השטר כשר, והא דתנן במתני' (לקמן בבא מציעא דף עה:) דעדים עוברין, היינו כשאין ניכר הרבית בשטר ויודעים עדים שיש בו רבית — דהא אהאי שטרא גופי' אמרי' בפרק המניח (ב"ק דף ל:) ובפרק המוכר פירות (ב"ב דף צד: ושם ד"ה וחכמים) דמשעת כתיבה עבד ליה שומא. וי"ל דאיירי הכא ברבית דרבנן, ולא מיפסלו באיסור דרבנן כיון שאין מרויחים כלום, אע"פ שבעבירה דאורייתא היו נפסלים. אי נמי, אפי' ברבית דאורייתא יש להכשיר, דשמא "לא תשימון" לאינשי במלוה משמע להו ולא בעדים, ולכך כשרים, כדאמרינן נמי (לעיל בבא מציעא דף ה:): "לא תחמוד" לאינשי בלא דמי משמע להו. אבל קשה ההיא דשטרי חוב המוקדמים: היאך העדים כשרים? דמוקמינן לה כר"מ, אבל לרבנן גובה מזמן שני, ולר"מ נמי היה גובה אי לאו משום דקניס, ורבי יוחנן נמי לא קאמר דפסולים לרבנן אלא משום גזירה שמא יגבה מזמן ראשון — והלא העדים הללו במתכוין חתמו שקר והקדימו את הזמן! וי"ל כגון שיש עדים שמעידין עליהם שהיו אנוסים מחמת נפשות, או כגון שאומרים: "טעינו בשנת המלך", אי נמי בשיפורא בין מלא בין חסר, ולא הזכירו בשטר בכמה בשבת אלא בכמה בחדש:
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 72a:6:1.english: "[In the case of] a promissory note in which there is interest, we penalize him, and he may not collect the principal and may not collect the interest" - Rivam explained that he cannot collect from encumbered property, but from unencumbered property he can collect on the basis of that note, since the witnesses are not disqualified, as they are not "witnesses of violence" [i.e., venal witnesses], for they gain nothing from the matter. And [this is] difficult, for it was taught in the Tosefta ([Chapter 5] of our tractate): "One who finds a promissory note in which there is interest must tear it up; if it comes before the court, they must tear it up." Now, if he can collect with it from unencumbered property, why should they tear it up? Let them wait until he first collects with it! And one can answer that it is forbidden to keep it. However, it seems that Rabbi Meir penalizes [him] completely and he cannot collect with it at all, just like antedated promissory notes, which we establish shortly below as [reflecting] Rabbi Meir's view. And even though there too Rashi explained that they are invalid only for collecting from encumbered property, [this] does not seem [correct], for "invalid" implies that he cannot collect with it at all. And as for that which [the Gemara] asks: "Granted that he cannot collect from the first date, let him collect from the second date," it could also have said: "Granted that he cannot collect from encumbered property, let him collect from unencumbered property," except that it asks a stronger question: that even from encumbered property he should be able to collect from the second date. And shortly below, where [the Gemara] asks regarding the incident of the orchard: "Rather, [regarding] that which Rabbi Yochanan said, 'It is a decree lest he collect from the first date,' let us say [that it is] because it was not meant to be written," and it does not answer that the reason of "it was not meant to be written" is effective only [to say] that he cannot collect from encumbered property — [that is] because it holds that it is certainly effective to invalidate it completely so that he cannot collect with it at all. And as for why [the Gemara there] only raises a question as to whether he can collect from encumbered property, whereas from unencumbered property it is obvious to it that he can collect even though it was not meant to be written — there, where it is obvious to it that he can collect, that is because the seller admitted to the buyer that he had not repaid [him]. And furthermore, it seems that even if there are other witnesses or the debtor admits [the debt], even so Rabbi Meir penalizes [him], for thus it implies that he does not collect the principal, similar to the interest. And in the Tosefta (there) as well it is implied that even in an oral loan he penalizes [him], as it teaches: "One who lends to his fellow with interest and comes before the court, they penalize him and he may not collect the principal and may not collect the interest, for Rabbi Meir used to say: A promissory note in which there is interest, etc." And in the chapter [entitled] Hamaniach (Bava Kamma 30b) as well, we compare [this] to that case where they penalized the principal because of their appreciation, where he forfeits the principal of the property, [so] likewise he penalizes [him] with respect to the principal of the loan — even though one could reject [this comparison, arguing] that there the transgression was committed with the principal of the property itself more than here, for here the main transgression is in the document, as we say there: "From the time of writing [the note], he made an assessment [of the interest]," and therefore they penalized only in [the case of] a document. However, [regarding] the Rabbis, it seems that they certainly did not penalize [him] at all, and it is implied on the surface that according to the Rabbis he collects the principal with the note even from encumbered property, and Rabbi Meir too disagrees only because he penalizes. And [this is] astonishing: Why are the witnesses not disqualified? Since they transgress "You shall not place [interest upon him]" (Exodus 22[:24]), even though they do not profit, they ought to be disqualified, just like a transgressor who eats non-kosher meat to provoke [God], regarding whom we hold (Sanhedrin 27a) in accordance with Abaye that he is disqualified! And as for [the fact] that [the Mishnah] does not list them in the chapter [entitled] Zeh Borer (Sanhedrin 24b), so too it does not list the borrower, rather he is included in "a loan that comes with interest," as it explains there: "a loan that comes with interest," and the same applies to witnesses as well [that they are] included. And one cannot explain [that our case is] where interest is not explicitly stated in the note, but rather it wrote generally "So-and-so owes So-and-so a maneh" and they included the principal together with the interest and the witnesses did not know — for if so, shortly below where Rabbi Yochanan says that the Rabbis agree regarding antedated promissory notes [that they are invalid as] a decree lest he collect from the first date, here too we should decree lest he collect interest under the guise of principal! And one also cannot say that since the interest is explicitly stated in the note, the witnesses do not transgress "You shall not place," because the witnesses know that the court will not collect interest through them and therefore the note is valid, and that which we learned in the Mishnah (below, Bava Metzia 75b) that the witnesses transgress [the prohibition] is when the interest is not recognizable in the note yet the witnesses know that there is interest in it — for regarding this very note itself we say in the chapter [entitled] Hamaniach (Bava Kamma 30b) and in the chapter [entitled] Hamocher Peirot (Bava Batra 94b, and there s.v. "VeChachamim") that from the time of writing [the note] he made an assessment [of the interest]. And one can answer that it is speaking here of rabbinic interest, and they are not disqualified for a rabbinic prohibition since they do not profit at all, even though for a biblical transgression they would be disqualified. Alternatively, even in [a case of] biblical interest one can validate [them], for perhaps "You shall not place" is understood by people [as applying] to the lender and not to the witnesses, and therefore they are valid, just as we also say (above, Bava Metzia 5b): "You shall not covet" is understood by people [as applying only to taking] without payment. However, that [case] of antedated promissory notes is difficult: how are the witnesses valid? For we establish it as [reflecting] Rabbi Meir's view, whereas according to the Rabbis he collects from the second date, and according to Rabbi Meir too he would collect were it not that he penalizes, and Rabbi Yochanan too says that they are invalid according to the Rabbis only because of a decree lest he collect from the first date — yet did these witnesses not intentionally sign a falsehood and antedate the date?! And one can answer [that it is] a case where there are witnesses testifying about them that they were coerced under threat to their lives, or a case where they say, "We erred in the regnal year," or alternatively regarding the proclamation [of the new month], whether [the previous month was] full or defective, and they did not mention in the note which day of the week [it was], only which day of the month.

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 72a:6:2.hebrew: קונסין אותו ואינו גובה וכו' - ואע"ג דאמרי' בפ' אע"פ (כתובות דף. ס:) הלכה כר"מ בגזירותיו, היינו דוקא בגזירותיו ולא בקנסותיו, והכא קנס הוא. דכה"ג נמי פסקו בהלכות [גדולות] כרבנן דר"מ במעוברת חבירו ומינקת חבירו, דאם נשא יוציא; לכשיגיע זמנו לכנוס, יכנוס, ולא כר"מ דאמר לא יחזיר עולמית (. סוטה דף כו.), דהוי קנסא. וראיה מדבעי בהחולץ (יבמות דף לז.): אם אינסבא לכהן, (לא) [אי] החמירו לגרש, כיון שאינו יכול לחזור ולכנוס, דגרושה אסורה לכהן [וע"ע תוס' זבחים קד. ד"ה א"ר עקיבא]:
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 72a:6:2.english: "We penalize him, and he may not collect, etc." - Even though we say in the chapter [entitled] Af Al Pi (Ketubot 60b) [that] the halakhah follows Rabbi Meir in his decrees, that is specifically in his decrees and not in his penalties, and here it is a penalty. For similarly, in Halakhot [Gedolot] they ruled like the Rabbis who dispute Rabbi Meir regarding a woman pregnant from another man or a woman nursing another man's child, that if [someone] married [her] he must divorce [her], [and] when his time arrives to marry [her], he may marry [her] — and not like Rabbi Meir who says he may never remarry [her] (Sotah 26a), because it is a penalty. And a proof [for this is] from what [the Gemara] asks in [the chapter entitled] HaCholetz (Yevamot 37a): if she was married to a kohen, did they rule stringently [that he must] divorce [her], since he cannot go back and marry [her], as a divorcée is forbidden to a kohen? [And see further Tosafot on Zevachim 104a, s.v. "Amar Rabbi Akiva".]
